correctness.rationale: For uniform S_n, nearby index/value pairs T_n have E T_n=O(1). Bond slide graph on two-deletion sets has rank loss (n−2)J−binom(J,2) when unit bonds do not share endpoints. Single-common deletion collisions reduce to monotone consecutive-value slides, with exceptional pairs bounded by T_n; disjoint deletions force four matched nearby indices and at most binom(2T_n,2)^2 extra edges. Overlapping bonds have probability O(1/n). Thus D_n−(n−2)J_n=O_P(1). Factorial moments of J_n ->2^r, so D_n/n -> Poisson(2).

evidence: Bevan–Homberger–Tenner characterize k-prolific permutations at every n via min Manhattan gap >=k+2, but do not quantify the typical shortfall when k=2. Homberger 2012 section 4 calculates only D_1 random mean/variance, section 5 extremal D_k.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Their general results cover exact zero-deficit geometry but not the random positive collision count or scaled Poisson distribution.

evidence: Bond graph on unordered two-deletion position sets has (n−2)J edges and exactly choose(J,2) square redundancies when bonds disjoint; all other equality collisions are bounded by O(T_n+T_n^4) with E[T_n]=O(1). Thus D_n/n−J_n->0 in probability and J_n->Pois(2).
